style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: On a weathered concrete workbench, a heavy glass hourglass stands at the far left third, its end caps warm oak and bone white; a machined graphite steel collar ring clamps tight around the narrow waist, its latch arm open in a hard clean edge. Beside it to the right, a rust-finish modular inspection gate lies unlatched, hinged open on a brushed steel base. One directional raking key light from the left throws a long cast shadow across the bench. Palette bone white, graphite, rust; extreme asymmetry with the hourglass off-centre on the left third and generous negative space on the right; no text, no lettering.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, numerals, typography
rationale: The article is a single tax rule with no physical facility, so component_assembly turns the abstract collision into a modular mechanical restraint. The hourglass gives time without numerals, and the collar ring names the exact option instrument that resets the clock.
cue: the put restarts the long-term holding clock
subject: a machined steel collar ring clamped around the waist of a heavy glass hourglass on a workbench, with an unlatched modular inspection gate beside it
core_thesis: A collar on employer stock is a short sale wrapped in a straddle: the put restarts the 12-month long-term holding clock, defers the put loss against unrealised gain, and disqualifies the dividend for the covered stretch.
core_conflict: Protection without selling versus losing qualified long-term capital gain and dividend treatment.
